name: RadioCard

examples.title: Basic Usage
examples.code:
<Radios label="Plan" name="plan" defaultValue="pro">
  <RadioCard
    value="starter"
    title="Starter"
    description="One site, community support."
  />
  <RadioCard value="pro" title="Pro" description="Ten sites, email support." />
  <RadioCard
    value="team"
    title="Team"
    description="Unlimited sites, a support plan."
  />
</Radios>

examples.title: Columns
examples.code:
<Radios label="Time" name="slot" defaultValue="10">
  <Grid minCol={10} flexGrow="1">
    {['9', '10', '11', '12', '13', '14'].map(hour => (
      <RadioCard
        key={hour}
        value={hour}
        hasIndicator={false}
        title={`${hour}:00`}
        description="Open"
      />
    ))}
  </Grid>
</Radios>

accessibility:
- The card is a `<label>` around a native `<input type="radio">`, so a click anywhere on it picks
  the radio and it sends its value with a form.
- Cards that share a `name` are one group to the browser: Tab lands on the picked card, or the
  first, and the arrow keys move and pick, skipping disabled cards. Give `Radios` a `name`, or
  each card the same one; without it each card is a group of its own.
- The radio is named by the title, through `aria-labelledby`, and described by the description,
  through `aria-describedby`. An `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` you pass wins. Without a title,
  the card's own text names it, as a label's text does.
- The children aren't read when the radio takes focus. Put what matters in `title` and
  `description`.
- A link inside the card is its own Tab stop, and following it doesn't pick the card. A button or
  another input can't go inside a `<label>`.
- Keyboard focus draws an outline around the whole card, in Bulma's focus color, whatever the
  card's color.
- The selection never rests on color: the radio shows it, and the picked card's edge is twice as
  thick, with or without the radio.
- Contrast: against the card, a picked edge in `primary` or `link` clears WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 on a
  light page, and in every color on a dark one. `info`, `success`, `warning` and `danger` fall
  short on a light page, where the edge's width and the radio still show the selection.
- In forced colors (Windows contrast themes), Bulma's card loses its shadow, so the edge is a
  real border there: the system's text color, `Highlight` and still thicker when picked, and gray
  when disabled. The radio takes system colors as `Radio`'s does, and the focus outline is
  `Highlight`.
- The edge and the radio change without a transition under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
summary: The `RadioCard` component is a radio button drawn as a card, with a title and a description, picked wherever you click it. It's a `<label>` around a real radio, so it sends its `value` with a form, and the cards that share a `name` are one choice the arrow keys move through. The title names the radio and the description describes it. Inside `Radios` it takes the group's name and selection, as `Radio` does.

parts.summary: The `RadioCard` component is a radio button drawn as a card, with a title and a description, picked wherever you click it. It's a `<label>` around a real radio, so it sends its `value` with a form, and the cards that share a `name` are one choice the arrow keys move through. The title names the radio and the description describes it. Inside `Radios` it takes the group's name and selection, as `Radio` does.

props.name: title
props.description: What the option is, such as "Express". It names the radio, so a screen reader says it with the state and its place in the group. Without it, the card's whole text names the radio, as a label's text does.

props.name: description
props.description: A line or two about the option, read after the name and the state. It's the radio's description when `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` names it. Without one of those it's part of the name already, so it isn't read twice.

props.name: children
props.description: Anything else in the card, after the description, such as a price. A label holds phrasing content only, so spans, images and links: a link works and doesn't pick the card, but a button or another input can't go inside a label at all. It isn't read when the radio takes focus, so put what a screen reader should hear in `title` and `description`.

props.name: hasIndicator
props.description: Shows the radio at the start of the card. Without it, the card's edge alone shows the selection, and it's thicker when picked, so the selection never rests on color.

props.name: color
props.description: The color of the radio and of a picked card's edge.

props.name: textColor
props.description: Text color helper, on the card. The title and the children take it, and the description keeps its own color.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the card is disabled. A disabled card dims, takes no clicks, and the arrow keys skip it.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes, on the outer `<label>`, the card. That's the element that declares the `--bulma-radio-card-*` variables, and Bulma's `--bulma-card-*` ones, so a class is how to set one: `style` and the other input attributes go to the `<input>`. Name `.radio-card` beside your class in the selector, so it beats the card's own declaration whatever order the stylesheets load in. A `color` prop declares the active color again on `.radio-card.is-<color>`, which ties that selector, so leave `color` unset when a class sets it.

extraProps.name: name
extraProps.description: The form field name, which the cards of one choice share, so the arrow keys move between them. Inside `Radios`, the group's `name` when this is unset.

extraProps.name: value
extraProps.description: What a form sends when this card is the one picked. Inside a `Radios` group that takes `value`, `defaultValue` or `onChange`, the card is checked while the group's value is this.

parts.catchAll: All standard <input> attributes and Bulma helper props
parts.helperPropsNote: Helper props go on the outer `<label>`, the `.card`, with `className`. The other attributes go on the `<input>`.
